observations: Approved canonical records require protected reference tokens and scoped gateway enforcement, without naming the native helper header.

Upstream helper tests explicitly exercise Proxy-Authorization bearer through unary gRPC, stream interception and object HTTP. Authorization rejection alone does not prove there is no native reference-token channel.
The helper delegates nonmatching object origins and the HTTP client controls redirects; the source does not enforce the exact-origin refusal required by the existing assertion seam.
Dolt go.mod declares Go1.27.3. This is a declared source toolchain, not a verified installed-binary build receipt.
Go1.27.3 treats both Authorization and Proxy-Authorization as sensitive, but default redirects allow host/subdomain credential copying without exact scheme/port comparison.
The upstream executable helper protocol test skips Windows and uses a POSIX shell. It does not provide native Windows protocol proof.
The stock helper executes a single configured executable with get; PowerShell script execution on Windows needs a supported argument-vector launch route.
inferences: A narrow client hardening patch can preserve the existing helper protocol and Dolt object algorithm, but must be selected before adoption and proven natively.
The prior standard-Authorization-only framing was an agent-added constraint, not an approved acceptance criterion.
Do not infer that a source seam, passing upstream test text or the existing 2730 mock cases establishes real token relay, exact-origin safety or readiness.
decisionStatus: Proposed alternatives; operator selection required before adopting a patched Dolt client or new native library host
